fa9b9d341efe: Make or break a verse span · translationCore 4 Help
f530bcc1d6ff: A verse span (also called a verse bridge) is two or more verses translated as one unit, for example 2-3.
95ad44313a34: Open the section with its Draft section {span} label, type the text, and click Place verse numbers.
3fcf8b283cb1: Click the later number in the text, for example 10.
ed04b4022fbd: Click the word where the earlier verse (9) begins. The tooltip says "Join verse 10 to verse 9 at …".
00965f803729: Click Save section. The verses are saved as one span, numbered 2-3.
8040a4812e1b: Open the section again, click Place verse numbers, click the 10 and click the word where verse 10 should begin. Then click Save section.
3a781f8fca28: In Type mode you can also start a line with the span, for example 2-3 ….
50b37754200f: Making or breaking a span marks the checks and alignments of those verses for review. Nothing is deleted. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned.
2a9614442c0b: Spans can't be made in Verse view.
e2cade4b6fa9: Open Bible Stories have frames, not verse numbers, so they have no spans.
fa2c6f1d53f1: Place verse numbers mode for Titus 2:9–10 after joining: the numbers 9 and 10 sit side by side on the first word, Exhorta, so the two verses are one span.
